findings.finding: On 2026-08-31, with July and August already booked, Herbalife reaffirmed Q3 guidance (net sales +0.5% to +4.5% reported, adj. EBITDA $160-180m, FX assumptions unchanged from Aug 5) and the CFO said the outlook 'remains firmly on track' and the company expects a fifth consecutive quarter of YoY sales growth; this year Q1 sales were pre-released above guide and Q2 sales ($1,326.8m, +5.4%) landed at the top of the range, so a print at or above the $1.31bn Street revenue number is the base case.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Sales beats have not been paid in 2026: Q2 (sales at top of guide) fell -8.65% on an EPS miss; Q1 sales above guide were pre-released 2026-04-14 (+7.34%) and the print itself fell -11.86%. Earlier, 2025-11-05 +11.65% and 2026-02-18 +18.32%.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the reaffirmation is public and on the wire. What is less visible is that it was made with two-thirds of the quarter in hand by a CFO who becomes interim CEO on Nov 1, which lowers the probability of a Q3 sales miss; if fully priced, Street revenue would sit at or above the $1.31bn guide upper half rather than at $1.30bn (earningswhispers) and the stock would not trade 10% below its post-Q2 high of $14.89. It lands inside the guided range, so it is sized small.
findings.independence: Q2 release shows sales at the top of the range (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001180262/000121390026085702/ea030059301ex99-1.htm); same company, different document.

findings.finding: The adj. EPS bar of $0.62-0.63 sits above what the guide midpoint implies: from the Q2 release, adj. EBITDA $166.6m less ~$37m net interest and ~$35m D&A/SaaS amortisation gave ~$94m adj. pretax; at the reaffirmed ~35% FY adj. tax rate and ~104.5m diluted shares, Q3 EBITDA of $160/170/180m maps to roughly $0.53/$0.60/$0.66, so $0.62-0.63 needs ~$173-176m (upper half), and the $0.73 consensus one preview quotes would need EBITDA above the top of the guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026: adj. EPS $0.51 vs $0.61-0.63 consensus, driven by a 43.2% adj. tax rate, stock -8.65% despite sales at the top of guide. Q3 2025: adj. EPS $0.50 vs $0.46 consensus, stock +11.65%.
findings.why_not_priced: This is arithmetic on public numbers that aggregators do not do; the 11% three-month cut in next-quarter EPS estimates (chartmill snippet) shows the Street moved part of the way, but if fully priced the consensus would sit near $0.60, not $0.62-0.73. It is my inference from the guide, not a company EPS guide (there is none), so it is sized small. The bar is disputed ($0.73 in one preview), which caps it.
findings.independence: Tax rate and interest figures also in the finviz preview (https://finviz.com/news/407924/herbalifes-india-engine-meets-its-gst-anniversary-as-street-bets-on-46-eps-growth, 2026-10-26), which quotes the $0.73/$0.76 numbers; FY ~35% adj. tax rate from the 2026-08-31 release. Same underlying company documents.

findings.finding: The reaffirmed FY guide (+2.5% to +5.5%, $5.16-5.32bn) after H1 growth of ~+6.6% and the Q3 range implies Q4 net sales of roughly flat YoY at the midpoint, while India (Q2 +33% reported, +47% cc on +45% volume) begins lapping its September 2025 GST cut and China (-29% cc) and EMEA (-5.6% cc) are still declining; the Q4/FY update on this print is the line most exposed to the India lap.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: 2026-08-05: FY adj. EBITDA guide narrowed down ($670-690m from $675-705m, FX) with sales range narrowed and midpoint raised; stock -8.65% (mixed with the EPS miss).
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: Street FY revenue $5.20bn is already in the lower half of the range (earningswhispers), so a hold of the FY guide is not a disappointment; the residual risk is a cut toward or below the low end if the India decelerates faster than the guide assumes. Net of the rest of the company: Asia Pacific ex-China (+23% cc) and LatAm (+8% cc) carry the growth; North America is flat.
findings.independence: Regional numbers from the Q2 release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001180262/000121390026085702/ea030059301ex99-1.htm); FY guide from the 2026-08-31 release. The Q4-implied arithmetic is mine.

findings.finding: This is the first print after the CEO change: Stephan Gratziani left the CEO role on 2026-10-31 and CFO John DeSimone, who had already announced his retirement as CFO effective 2026-12-31 (successor Scott Schaefer from 2027-01-01), is interim CEO from 2026-11-01 with no permanent successor named; the call will be led by an interim team with two finance transitions under way.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior print under interim leadership in the baseline window. The 2026-08-31 announcement coincided with the guidance reaffirmation; the stock's reaction that day is not sourced here.
findings.why_not_priced: Public for two months and probably mostly priced; what is not yet known is whether the call names a successor, sets a 2027 frame, or stays silent on strategy, which is a source of variance more than of sign. The guide-setter is now the CEO, which argues for continuity of the conservative guide.
findings.independence: CFO transition in the Q2 release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001180262/000121390026085702/ea030059301ex99-1.htm); EDGAR shows the 8-K item 5.02 of 2026-08-31 and no Form 4 since 2026-08-05 (https://www.sec.gov/cgi-bin/browse-edgar?action=getcompany&CIK=0001180262&type=&dateb=&owner=include&count=40).

findings.finding: On 2026-09-08 the board authorised a $250m buyback over three years (about 18% of a ~$1.38bn market cap at $13.21), the first since the deleveraging; the Q3 release and 10-Q will show whether any shares were bought in September and the intended pace, against a stated aim of net leverage below 2x by year-end (2.2x at June 30).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The authorisation itself lifted the stock more than 6% pre-market on 2026-09-08 (rttnews summary via search); no prior print has carried a buyback update in the baseline window.
findings.why_not_priced: The authorisation is priced (the +6% move). What is not is execution: a print showing meaningful September repurchases or an accelerated pace would be new; one showing none, with leverage still above 2x, would be neutral. Sized small.
findings.independence: Q2 release gives cash $370.5m and net leverage 2.2x (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001180262/000121390026085702/ea030059301ex99-1.htm); no insider Form 4 purchases since 2026-08-05 on EDGAR.

findings.finding: FX moved roughly as the guide assumed: the guide used average rates from the first two weeks of July 2026, and over Q3 the DXY was about +0.2% with EUR/USD -0.3% (broker table, Oct 2026), USD/INR at ~96.2 in late September (a nine-week low, 'lowest since July'), and the ECB-reference EUR/INR 108.82 and EUR/MXN 20.58 on Sep 30, so no FX gap to the reported range in Q3; the late-September dollar rebound is a small headwind to a Q4 guide reset at October rates.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: 2026-08-05 FY EBITDA guide narrowed down primarily on FX; stock -8.65% (mixed with the EPS miss).
findings.why_not_priced: A macro-to-company proxy the company has not confirmed; filed small. If the market had a large FX miss priced, Street revenue would sit below the guide midpoint, and it sits at or above it.
findings.independence: Rupee level: https://tradingeconomics.com/india/currency/news/587335 ; Sep 30 reference rates: https://www.boe.es/boe/dias/2026/10/01/pdfs/BOE-A-2026-20464.pdf . Proxy only.
